site.name: Lincoln Mine
site.location: Bummer Gulch / Sugar Loaf Mining District
overview: Lincoln Mine is a documented historic gold mine with tungsten mineralization in Bummer Gulch, within Boulder County's Sugar Loaf mining area.
State records place the workings in the southeast quarter of Section 30, Township 1 North, Range 71 West and describe a creek-bottom shaft, a 60-foot tunnel, and surface cuts.

timeline.text: The Engineering and Mining Journal reported that the Lincoln Mining, Milling and Development Company was installing an air-compressor plant and boiler in Bummer Gulch and planned to use Sullivan air drills; N. M. Nelson was manager.
Colorado Geological Survey records listed James McGlaghan as owner, reported 1,250 units of production, and described the property as primarily a gold mine with tungsten occurring in a cross vein.

moreHistory: Colorado Geological Survey records describe the Lincoln workings as a shaft in the creek bottom, a 60-foot tunnel, and surface cuts in granite.

Carnegie Library for Local History preserves two photographs identified as the Lincoln Mine and tunnel in Bummer Gulch, with ore cars visible, independently corroborating the named mine and tunnel component.
The map point is a representative location within the documented southeast quarter of Section 30 in Bummer Gulch. It should not be read as a field-surveyed surviving shaft or tunnel entrance.
